scope: Proposition 10.1 (Remaining first-join comparisons) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 74. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a finite block and the retained centres, masks, and table operations of Sections 3–9, with the stated parameter hierarchy. At each first sharing of a component, omit the simultaneous-birth comparisons already treated in Section 7. For the remaining comparisons, the following estimates hold uniformly over the permitted prior table history. 1. The sum of broad pair counts in λ ⊗ λ, at distance at most Crmax and with width weight rmin, is O(1). Here C is any fixed positive constant. 2. The same-width, same-remaining-mask counts in common new cells, weighted by the single factor riπI(a) and the product of the two raw weights, have total O(W) + Ok0 (W1+c ) for some fixed c > 0. The constants are independent of the slot cap N0 and of the finite block. Thus, together with the direct comparisons, these estimates establish Proposition 5.2.
